SAMPLE: Reading a sealed Herculaneum scroll with machine learning
SAMPLE page, invented for tests and never fetched. Hundreds of papyrus scrolls from the library at Herculaneum were charred by the eruption of Mount Vesuvius in AD 79 and cannot be unrolled. We scanned one sealed scroll with X-rays and flattened its layers in software. We trained a machine-learning model to detect ink. The model was trained on small patches where ink had been found by hand. We read about 1,800 Greek letters in six columns of text. Scholars in two countries, outside our group, checked the readings. The text is a prose work on friendship. Open access. This article is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License. DOI 10.1038/nature-ut-sample-0001.

SAMPLE: Tiles that fill the plane only without repeating
SAMPLE page, invented for tests and never fetched. Two mathematicians at Eastvale University prove that tiles of one kind can fill the flat plane only in patterns that never repeat. The question has been open since 1968. The proof runs to 38 pages and needs no computer search. We prove the result for tilings of the plane. The three-dimensional case remains open. Tilings appear in computer science and in the study of materials. DOI 10.1017/ut-sample-0013.
